note: Shared inventory vectors. The backend's InventoryEditor (xUnit) and, for scope shared only, Unity's InventorySession (EditMode) must agree on every case. Written by hand from Unity's rules (InventorySession, ItemTransfer, ItemInventory, OperativeEquipment, InventoryState) plus the owner's backend rulings (spec S5-D1 exact transfers, S5-D7 retired items), never generated by running either implementation. Each case is self-contained: bagCapacity, the items it needs (a definition absent from items is retired; only scope backend uses one), operatives (labels such as op1), the initial state, the operations, and either the expected state or the first refusal. A state has the stash and one bag per operative: instances as [label, definitionId] (labels stand for item ids so each runner maps them to its own ids; a label names one non-stackable item and is unique in the case), stacks as [definitionId, totalQuantity] (one total per location and definition; a bag shows ceil(total / maxStack) entries, so Unity splits a total into entries of maxStack with the one open entry last), and per bag the equipped label per slot (weapon, armor, utility; null when empty). Instances, then stacks, are the order Unity creates the entries in. Operations: equip {operative, item}; unequip {operative, slot}; toStash and toBag {operative, item} for an instance or {operative, definition, quantity} for units of a stack, always about that operative's bag; equipFromStash {operative, item}. The special labels ghost (an item that exists nowhere) and opX (an operative not in the case) may appear in operations only. Expected is {state} or {refused: {index, code}} where index is the zero-based position of the first refused operation, code is an InventoryRefusal name, and a refused batch changes nothing. Scope shared: both runners run it, so it uses only what Unity does identically (it never asks for more than is held, never hits partial room, never uses an unknown operative on toStash or toBag where Unity says NotFound, never involves a retired definition, never starts over capacity). Scope backend: xUnit only, and the why string names the reason (strict quantities, unknown operatives on transfers, retired definitions, over-capacity bags that Unity's public API cannot build).

cases.name: strict-more-than-held-to-the-bag-is-insufficient
cases.why: S5-D1: the backend moves exactly the requested quantity or fails; Unity clamps a request to what the entry holds

cases.name: strict-more-than-held-to-the-stash-is-insufficient
cases.why: S5-D1: the backend moves exactly the requested quantity or fails; Unity clamps a request to what the entry holds

cases.name: strict-more-than-held-across-two-bag-entries-is-insufficient
cases.why: S5-D1: the backend sums a definition's units at a location (one row); Unity addresses one entry and would move only part

cases.name: strict-a-stack-needing-one-more-entry-than-free-is-refused
cases.why: S5-D1: the bag has 2 free entries of 3, so Unity would move the 6 units that fit and leave 4 in the stash; the backend refuses the whole request

cases.name: strict-one-unit-over-the-exact-fill-is-refused
cases.why: S5-D1: 6 units fill the 2 free entries exactly (shared case to-bag-a-stack-that-fills-the-bag-leaves-the-remainder-in-the-stash); the 7th needs a third entry and Unity would move 6 and leave 1

cases.name: strict-an-open-entry-plus-new-entries-beyond-the-free-ones-is-refused
cases.why: S5-D1: 1 unit tops up the open entry and 3 fill the free one, so Unity would move 4 of 5; the backend refuses the whole request

cases.name: strict-batch-refuses-the-second-stack-move-by-quantity
cases.why: S5-D1: after the first move the stash holds 7 and 8 are asked for; Unity would clamp to what the entry holds

cases.name: stack-with-no-row-in-the-bag-is-not-found
cases.why: stacks are addressed by definition and location; Unity addresses an entry by instance id

cases.name: stack-with-no-row-in-the-stash-is-not-found
cases.why: stacks are addressed by definition and location; Unity addresses an entry by instance id

cases.name: to-bag-a-negative-quantity-is-invalid
cases.why: pins the backend's handling of a negative quantity, an input the API's request validation would normally refuse earlier; Unity's own handling (InvalidQuantity for any value below 1) is covered by the shared case to-stash-quantity-zero-is-invalid

cases.name: unknown-operative-to-the-stash-with-an-instance
cases.why: S5-D8: a missing operative is UnknownOperative; Unity's InventoryState.MoveToStash reports NotFound for it

cases.name: unknown-operative-to-the-stash-with-a-stack
cases.why: S5-D8: a missing operative is UnknownOperative; Unity's InventoryState.MoveToStash reports NotFound for it

cases.name: unknown-operative-to-the-bag-with-an-instance
cases.why: S5-D8: a missing operative is UnknownOperative; Unity's InventoryState.MoveToBag reports NotFound for it

cases.name: unknown-operative-to-the-bag-with-a-stack
cases.why: S5-D8: a missing operative is UnknownOperative; Unity's InventoryState.MoveToBag reports NotFound for it

cases.name: retired-instance-cannot-be-equipped
cases.why: S5-D7: a definition the catalogue no longer knows (item.relic) may leave a bag but not be equipped; Unity's own unknown-item handling is separate

cases.name: retired-instance-cannot-go-from-the-stash-to-a-bag
cases.why: S5-D7: a retired definition (item.relic) may leave a bag but not enter one

cases.name: retired-instance-cannot-be-equipped-from-the-stash
cases.why: S5-D7: a retired definition (item.relic) may leave a bag but not enter one or be equipped

cases.name: retired-equipped-instance-must-be-unequipped-before-the-stash
cases.why: S5-D7: a retired definition (item.relic) is still an equipped item, so toStash is refused Equipped like any other

cases.name: retired-instance-unequipped-then-to-the-stash
cases.why: S5-D7: a retired definition (item.relic) can be recovered from a bag through unequip then toStash; Unity refuses transfers of unknown items

cases.name: retired-stack-to-the-stash-whole
cases.why: S5-D7: a retired definition (item.scrap) may leave a bag; Unity refuses transfers of unknown items

cases.name: retired-stack-to-the-stash-in-part
cases.why: S5-D7: a partial move of a retired definition (item.scrap) is allowed; the remainder still takes one bag entry

cases.name: retired-stack-merges-into-a-stash-row
cases.why: S5-D7: units of a retired definition (item.scrap) leaving a bag merge into the stash row of that definition

cases.name: retired-stack-cannot-go-from-the-stash-to-a-bag
cases.why: S5-D7: a retired definition (item.scrap) may leave a bag but not enter one

cases.name: retired-stack-takes-one-bag-entry-and-fills-a-full-bag
cases.why: S5-D7: a retired definition's maximum stack is unknown, so its row (40 units) counts as exactly one bag entry

cases.name: retired-stack-takes-one-bag-entry-and-leaves-room
cases.why: S5-D7: a retired definition's row (40 units) counts as one entry, so a bag of three has one entry left

cases.name: retired-items-do-not-trap-bag-capacity
cases.why: S5-D7: a retired instance (item.relic) in a full bag is sent to the stash, freeing the entry for a known item

cases.name: over-capacity-bag-can-still-send-an-instance-to-the-stash
cases.why: a catalogue that lowers bagCapacity leaves a bag over it (3 entries in a bag of 2); Unity's public API cannot build that state

cases.name: over-capacity-bag-can-still-equip
cases.why: a catalogue that lowers bagCapacity leaves a bag over it (3 entries in a bag of 2); equipping does not grow the bag

cases.name: over-capacity-bag-can-still-unequip
cases.why: a catalogue that lowers bagCapacity leaves a bag over it (3 entries in a bag of 2); unequipping does not grow the bag

cases.name: over-capacity-bag-refuses-an-instance
cases.why: a catalogue that lowers bagCapacity leaves a bag over it (3 entries in a bag of 2); an over-capacity bag may not grow

cases.name: over-capacity-bag-refuses-equip-from-the-stash
cases.why: a catalogue that lowers bagCapacity leaves a bag over it (3 entries in a bag of 2); an over-capacity bag may not grow

cases.name: over-capacity-bag-accepts-units-into-an-open-stack
cases.why: a catalogue that lowers bagCapacity leaves a bag over it (3 entries in a bag of 2); units that fit an open entry add no entry

cases.name: over-capacity-bag-refuses-units-needing-a-new-entry
cases.why: a catalogue that lowers bagCapacity leaves a bag over it (3 entries in a bag of 2); units that need a new entry would grow it

cases.name: over-capacity-bag-at-exactly-capacity-is-full
cases.why: a catalogue that lowers bagCapacity leaves a bag over it; one send to the stash brings it to exactly 2 entries, which is full, so the next toBag is refused

cases.name: over-capacity-bag-back-under-capacity-takes-a-new-instance
cases.why: a catalogue that lowers bagCapacity leaves a bag over it (3 entries in a bag of 2); once two entries are sent away there is room again
